newsitem.title: UK: Dollar keeps to steady path ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar keeps to steady path ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: The dollar continued to follow its steady path into the European midsession, marking time ahead of U.S. producer price and retail sales data due at 1230 GMT.
The dollar was steady against the mark and slightly firmer on the yen but still within the day's narrow ranges.
Dealers said activity was light ahead of the data and was likely to remain subdued into the long U.S. weekend.

"After having taken its eye off U.S. inflation risks over the last week, the market could be in for a small shock if the prices data starts to turn higher now," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank.
September producer price data is expected to show a 0.3 percent monthly rise with core prices up 0.2 percent.
The consensus forecast for retail sales points to a monthly rise of 0.2 percent with the ex-autos figure rising 0.3 percent.

Dealers said today's data is likely to show inflationary pressure is still low but market attention has already turned to next Wednesday's consumer price data. This will provide a better picture of the inflationary outlook and a better indication over U.S. monetary policy.
The dollar against the mark was trading at 1.5290/00 at 1056 GMT against 1.5294/04 late Thursday in Europe.
Against the yen, the dollar was trading at 111.45/50 from 111.24/29 late Thursday.
Sterling took centre stage in European trade as it pushed to fresh 20-month highs against the mark, testing territory above 2.41 marks.
Analysts attributed the pound's buoyancy mostly to UK Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's upbeat speech on the UK economy at the ruling Conservative party conference on Thursday.
Sterling/mark stood at 2.4105/08 at 1108 GMT against 2.3940/45 late Thursday.
